Cruz squeezes his nose to feel cartilage, works the grabber arm to lift the Megalodon tooth, shouts \"A hammerhead!\" and spots the great white. Phoenix notices \"There aren't any trees,\" names the \"nightlight shark,\" holds Cruz's hand and makes the Tooth Fairy joke. No likes or notes were in the brief, so none could be used.","craft":"It has a cold open at the bedroom LEGO build, and the glowing brick launches the adventure. The chapters climb through deep time from the first sharks to today, each with a beat (nose-squeeze, table-shark, tooth grab, walking shark, great white). It ends with a tooth keepsake and an \"Older than dinosaurs / Older than TREES\" callback.","facts":"The facts are almost all correct and well woven in: Greenland shark lifespan, cartilage, whale-shark spots, epaulette walking and conveyor-belt teeth. Two slips go unflagged: Helicoprion is presented as a shark though it was a relative of ratfish, and the great white \"can smell a tiny drop of blood from very far away\" repeats a popular exaggeration.","age_fit":"At 1851 words it is over the 1700 target but inside the 15% tolerance. The sound words, repetition and shout-lines suit band A, and the older child gets hooks like Helicoprion and the electric sense. However, the hushed \"Why is everybody hiding?\" Megalodon build-up, the great white's \"Rows and rows of teeth!\" and a mention of blood edge toward peril for a 4-year-old.","continuity":"The magic red brick glows and clicks to start the adventure and returns the boys home. It opens by recalling the LEGO adventure, keeps WHOOOOSH, and turns \"Play well\" into \"Swim well.\" Grandpa Greenie is one strong new recurring guide with a built-in reason to return.","delight":"There are lovely lines to read aloud (\"The Tooth Fairy must be SO busy,\" \"Yuck!\" said Phoenix, delighted), and the ending is warm. Chapters 5 and 6 sag into Grandpa Greenie monologues, though, with \"said Grandpa Greenie\" repeated over and over and a preachy conservation speech."},"caps_applied":["none"],"disqualified":false,"overall":4.5,"editor_notes":["Soften the band-A peril. Drop the 'everybody hiding' dread and the blood-smell line, and let the Megalodon and great-white moments land as wonder rather than suspense.","Break up Grandpa Greenie's longer speeches in Chapters 5-6 into back-and-forth with the boys (let them guess what the tiger shark ate, or spot the plankton), and trim the repeated 'said Grandpa Greenie' tags.","Fix or hedge Helicoprion ('a shark cousin with a spiral of teeth'), and make the smelling-blood fact accurate or cut it. Then clarify whether the keepsake is a Megalodon tooth so the callback pays off exactly."],"best_moment":"\"The Tooth Fairy must be SO busy,\" said Phoenix. Grandpa Greenie laughed so hard that bubbles came out of his gills.","worst_moment":"\"Great whites are amazing hunters,\" said Grandpa Greenie. \"They can smell a tiny drop of blood from very far away.\""}
